claims.text: Superconductivity in high-entropy alloys is primarily governed by the degree of local chemical ordering induced by substitution.
Increasing local chemical order raises the superconducting transition temperature.
Increasing local chemical order enhances the coherence of electron-phonon coupling.
Targeted elemental substitution followed by thermal treatment can promote partial chemical ordering in a high-entropy alloy.
Enhanced local order improves the spatial uniformity of electron-phonon coupling.
Enhanced local order increases the strength of electron-phonon coupling.
More uniform and stronger electron-phonon coupling facilitates Cooper pairing.
Facilitated Cooper pairing produces a higher superconducting transition temperature.
A fully chemically disordered structure introduces scattering.
Scattering caused by full chemical disorder suppresses superconductivity.
Samples subjected to the ordering intervention will have a higher superconducting transition temperature than the disordered baseline.
The increase in transition temperature will be greatest at substitution concentrations that optimize local order without causing phase separation.
The proposed effect is significant only within a narrow range of substitution levels and thermal-treatment parameters.
Excessive substitution or ordering may produce secondary phases.
Excessive substitution or ordering may diminish the proposed electron-phonon-coupling benefit.
